page.title: Overlays
page.description: OBS Browser Source chat overlays - a public, read-only, filtered view of your chat for the stream itself. For the private operator view, see Chat.

url.rotateConfirmBody: The current Browser Source URL stops working immediately. You'll need to paste the new one into OBS. No other settings are affected.

setup.title: OBS Browser Source setup
setup.step2: Create or choose an overlay profile here.
setup.step3: Copy its Browser Source URL above.
setup.step4: In OBS, add a new Browser Source to your scene.
setup.step5: Paste the URL into the Browser Source's URL field.
setup.step6: Set Width/Height to match your canvas (1920×1080 for a horizontal layout, 1080×1920 for vertical) - OBS scales the source, so this is a recommendation, not a requirement.
setup.step7: Leave Custom CSS empty - the overlay is already styled by its own settings.
setup.step8: The overlay is transparent by design; no background color is needed in OBS.
setup.step9: The overlay never needs any of OBS's Browser Source page permissions (camera, microphone, screen capture, etc.) - it only reads chat.
setup.step10: "Shutdown source when not visible" and "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" are both optional; leaving them off keeps the overlay connected and its recent messages visible when you switch scenes. See the documentation for the trade-offs.
setup.step11: On reconnect, the overlay restores whatever the server still retains - very old gaps are not backfilled; see the gap notice below.
setup.step12: A gap warning appears here in the management UI, never as large text on the live overlay itself.
